newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end slightly higher in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end slightly higher in thin trading.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed slightly higher on Wednesday as the focus moved from unlinked to CPI-linked bonds, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.05 pct to 100.8
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.02 pct to 100.49.
Volume was a low 92 million shekels, with trading in Makams falling to only 24 million shekels.
"Investors are focusing on the stock market so activity in the bond market is falling. Unlinked bonds continue to rise but at a much slower pace," said Eyal Kolka at Sigma Securities.
"The market made a very nice move before the end of the year and unlinked bonds are less attractive now," added a trader at Bank Hapoalim.

"CPI-linked long bonds continue to rise because investors prefer them over unlinked bonds," said Ron Weisberg of IBI Investment House. "The main reasons for the rise in the long bonds are expectations for declining 1997 inflation and a lowering of interest rates."
Traders noted that the rise of the Makam was minimal with activity falling sharply.
Traders said dollar-linked bonds declined mildly following the rise of the shekel against the dollar on Tuesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
